title: Scalar cup product naturality in coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. Use scalar cohomology, its recorded derived-functor coefficient maps, and its Ext-defined cup product [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. For $F,G,F\prime,G\prime\in X.\mathrm{Modules}$, morphisms $\varphi:F\to F\prime$, $\psi:G\to G\prime$, degrees $p,q\in\mathbb N$ and classes $a\in H_k^p(X,F)$, $b\in H_k^q(X,G)$, one has $H_k^{p+q}(\varphi\otimes\psi)(a\smile b)=H_k^p(\varphi)(a)\smile H_k^q(\psi)(b)$. There is no quasi-coherence assumption.

source.place: Cohomology Tags 01F7, 01FD, 07MB, 0FKV; Modules Tag 01CD for the normalized tensor-pullback map. Official sources https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F7 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FKV

proof.text: Use scalarCohomologyExtEquiv_map to identify each recorded coefficient map with postcomposition by mk₀ of scalarHom. This is the existing injective-resolution comparison naturality theorem; no new comparison choice is made.

Prove exact-functor Ext naturality for a natural transformation by induction on the Ext degree. In degree zero use mk₀_bijective and ordinary naturality. In positive degree take an injective presentation of the target, use covariant_sequence_exact₁ and vanishing of positive Ext into the injective object to express the class as composition with extClass. Apply mapExactFunctor_comp, mapExactFunctor_extClass and extClass_naturality to the mapped short exact sequences, followed by the induction hypothesis and Ext associativity. Mathlib GrothendieckAxioms.Sheaf, ModuleCat.AB and GrothendieckCategory.EnoughInjectives supply enough injectives for sheaves of k-vector spaces. Apply this lemma to curriedTensor.map of the first coefficient morphism; functoriality handles the second. Expand scalarExtCup and reassociate the Yoneda compositions to obtain Ext cup naturality.

Prove the scalarTensorCoefficient square by the sheafification adjunction. Express Sheaf.tensorLeftIso through inverse counit components and the lax monoidal tensor comparison. Counit naturality and μ_natural give the square for the tensor source. The adjunction reduces the remaining square to presheaf tensor extensionality, where tensorHom_app_tmulSection says both paths send s tensor t to φ(s) tensor ψ(t).

Apply injectivity of scalarCohomologyExtEquiv in degree p+q. Expand scalarCohomologyCup, cancel apply_symm_apply, and rewrite all coefficient maps using the comparison theorem. Combine the tensor-coefficient square with Ext cup naturality using mk₀_comp_mk₀ and comp_assoc_of_third_deg_zero. This proves the original equality in every degree.

mathlib_searches.query: Naturality of cup product on sheaf cohomology under coefficient maps
Cohomology cup product commutes with pullback and coefficient morphisms
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about group-cohomology coefficient maps; none states scalar scheme-module cup naturality. A separate coefficient-naturality query also returned group cohomology and nonabelian H1, no match.
One generic Ext transport hit, useful composition algebra but no scalar cup or normalized tensor-pullback compatibility.

Mathlib search via msearch: zero hits. Local searches of both library roots and DAG found moduleCup_coefficient_naturality and moduleCup_pullback_naturality in Sheaf.Paper.CechCupPullbackCompat; these require quasicoherent coefficients and IsModuleCupProduct rather than the scalar Ext-defined cup. They cannot apply to arbitrary coefficients here. Blueprint search for cup product naturality returned no matching node.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarCup_coefficient_naturality
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (F G F' G' : X.Modules)
    (φ : F ⟶ F') (ψ : G ⟶ G') (p q : ℕ)
    (a : scalarCohomology f F p) (b : scalarCohomology f G q) :
    scalarCohomologyMap f (@id ((F ⊗ G) ⟶ (F' ⊗ G')) (φ ⊗ₘ ψ)) 
        (p + q) (scalarCohomologyCup f F G p q a b) =
      scalarCohomologyCup f F' G' p q
        (scalarCohomologyMap f φ p a) (scalarCohomologyMap f ψ q b)
